transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I’ve been having these thoughts that are hard to shake. Like if I miss one setting, or one access rule, or some warning sign, then someone could get hurt or lose everything. I know that probably sounds excessive, and part of me does know it’s not completely rational, but in the moment it feels like it’s on me personally. Like I’m responsible, and I can’t just move on from it.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking or doing something to try and get rid of these thoughts?

Yes… I do. I mean, I try to tell myself it’s just being thorough, because in my job that’s not a bad thing, right? But it goes past that sometimes.

I’ll reread deployment plans or audit logs again and again, and I’ll check things like door locks too. Sometimes I go back through old messages, like I’m looking for something I missed. And I’ll count through steps in my head until they feel… safe, I guess. That sounds a little strange saying it out loud.

There have been nights where I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone else leaves because if I stop before it feels complete, I start to panic. I know that’s probably more than normal checking.
Do these checking behaviors interfere with your daily life or relationships in any way?

Yeah… it has, unfortunately. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely falling apart, but it’s definitely started affecting things.

At work, I missed a major cloud migration deadline because I just couldn’t get myself to finish signing off on decisions. I kept needing to check and re-check before I could say, “Yes, this is okay.” And now my team has kind of started working around me instead of relying on me, which… doesn’t feel great to admit.

Outside of work, I’ve stopped showing up for basketball and salsa nights. I tell myself I’m just busy or tired, but honestly I think I’ve lost some of the routines and people that used to keep me grounded. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel a strong need to arrange things in a specific order or symmetry?

I don’t think so… not in a strong way, at least. I mean, I like things organized, especially at work, but I wouldn’t say I’m driven by symmetry or needing objects lined up a certain way.

Unless I’m misunderstanding what you mean? I’m trying to answer it correctly. It’s more that I notice when something seems off, but I don’t think I have a specific ordering thing.
Do you experience any disturbing or unwanted thoughts or images that pop into your mind?

Yes… I do. I was hoping maybe it was just normal concern, because with my work there are real risks if something is missed. But it feels bigger than that.

What brings me in is that I keep getting these thoughts like, if I miss one setting, or one access rule, or some warning sign, someone could get hurt or lose everything. And even when part of me knows that’s probably not realistic, it hits me like I’m personally responsible.

It’s not like I want to think about it. It just pops in and then I can’t really move on from it. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like these checking behaviors are done to prevent something bad from happening?

Yes… I think that’s basically what it is. I don’t do it because I enjoy it or because I’m trying to be difficult. It feels like if I stop too soon, something bad could happen and it would be my fault.

So I’ll reread deployment plans, audit logs, access settings… even old messages, honestly, more times than I probably need to. And it’s not just work stuff. I’ve checked door locks over and over too. Sometimes I’m counting through the steps in my head until it feels… I don’t know, “safe” enough to move on.

I’m a little embarrassed saying this, but I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone else leaves because stopping before it feels complete makes me panic. I know that probably sounds excessive. I’m not trying to be dramatic — it just feels like I’m preventing something terrible from slipping through.
Do you feel relieved after completing these checking behaviors, like you've prevented something bad from happening?

Yes… I think I do feel relieved, at least for a little while. Like if I’ve reread the deployment plan enough times, or gone back through audit logs or access settings, then I can sort of tell myself, okay, I didn’t miss it.

It’s not really a good relief, though. It’s more like the panic drops enough that I can leave or move on. Sometimes with door locks or even old messages, I’ll keep checking and counting through the steps in my head until it feels “safe,” if that makes sense.

I know that probably sounds excessive. I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone else has gone because stopping before it feels complete makes me panic. But yes, when I finally finish, it does feel like I’ve prevented something bad… or at least like I’ve done enough for the moment.
How much distress do these thoughts and checking behaviors cause you on a daily basis?

It’s… pretty distressing, honestly. I mean, I try to tell myself it’s just being careful, especially at work, but it takes over a lot of the day.

I’ll reread deployment plans and audit logs and access settings again and again, and then sometimes I’m checking door locks or even old messages the same way. I’ll count through the steps in my head until it feels “safe,” which sounds strange saying out loud.

The worst part is when I can’t stop. I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone else leaves because leaving before it feels complete makes me panic. So… daily, I’d say it’s more than just annoying. It really wears me down. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any significant problems in your relationships with family or friends due to these thoughts and checking behaviors?

Yeah… somewhat. I mean, I don’t think anyone has, like, abandoned me or anything, but I’ve definitely pulled back.

I used to go to basketball regularly, and salsa nights too, and I’ve stopped showing up for those. At first I told myself I was just busy or tired, but it’s become a pattern. Those were kind of the routines — and people — that kept me grounded, so losing that hasn’t been great.

And at work… I guess this isn’t exactly family or friends, but it affects the people around me. I missed a major cloud migration deadline because I couldn’t finish signing off on decisions. My team has started working around me instead of relying on me, which is… hard to admit. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but yes, it’s causing problems. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking about?
Do you ever feel the need to repeat certain actions a specific number of times?

Yeah… I think so. Not always an exact number like “three times” or something, but I’ll sort of count through the steps in my head until it feels right or safe.

Like with deployment plans or audit logs, I’ll reread them over and over, and sometimes with door locks or even old messages I do the same kind of thing. I tell myself I’m just being thorough, but if I stop before it feels complete, I get really anxious.

I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone else has left because I couldn’t make myself stop checking. I know that probably sounds excessive… but yes, there is definitely a repeating-and-counting part to it. Is that what you mean?
Do you feel like these thoughts and checking behaviors are trying to prevent something harmful from happening to yourself or others?

Yes… I think that’s probably the main fear, even if I don’t like saying it that dramatically.

It’s like, if I miss one setting, or one access rule, or some warning sign, then something really bad could happen — someone could get hurt, or lose everything — and somehow it feels like it would be my fault. Part of me knows that’s not completely rational, or at least that the level of responsibility I’m feeling is probably too much.

But in the moment, it doesn’t feel optional. It feels like I have to keep checking so I’m not the reason something goes wrong. Does that make sense?
Have you had to take time off work or significantly reduce your work responsibilities due to these thoughts and checking behaviors?

I haven’t officially taken time off, exactly… or, I guess not in a formal way. But my responsibilities have definitely been affected.

I missed a major cloud migration deadline because I just couldn’t get myself to sign off on decisions. I kept feeling like I needed to be more certain before I approved anything. Since then, my team has started kind of working around me instead of relying on me the way they used to, which is embarrassing to say.

And outside of work, I’ve also stopped showing up for basketball and salsa nights, so I’m losing some of the routines and people that used to keep me grounded. So… maybe not “reduced responsibilities” officially, but in practice, yes, it’s definitely gotten in the way. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you considered that your checking behaviors might be causing more problems than they're solving, in terms of your work and personal life?

Yeah… I mean, I’ve started to wonder that. I still want to believe the checking is me being responsible, but it’s hard to ignore that it’s costing me things.

I missed that major cloud migration deadline because I couldn’t quite finish signing off on decisions, and since then my team has kind of started working around me instead of relying on me the same way. I don’t love admitting that.

And personally… I’ve stopped showing up for basketball and salsa nights, which used to be good for me. So I guess the checking is maybe giving me a temporary feeling of safety, but it’s also taking away routines and people that helped keep me grounded. Is that… the kind of problem you’re asking about?
Have these thoughts and checking behaviors significantly impacted your ability to enjoy or participate in activities you used to find pleasurable?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it has changed things.

I’ve stopped showing up for basketball and salsa nights, which used to be things I actually looked forward to. They gave me structure, and I saw people there. Now I just… don’t go, and then it’s easier to stay stuck in the same loop.

And at work, it’s affected me too. I missed a major cloud migration deadline because I couldn’t finish signing off on decisions, and since then my team has kind of started working around me instead of relying on me. That’s been hard to admit.

So yes, I guess it’s definitely interfering with things I used to enjoy and feel good about. Is that what you mean?
Do you feel compelled to perform any specific rituals or behaviors in a precise manner to reduce your anxiety?

Yeah… I think I do. I mean, I try to tell myself it’s just being thorough, but it does feel like there’s a certain way I have to do it or I can’t relax.

With deployment plans, I’ll reread them over and over, and check audit logs repeatedly. It’s not always that I find anything new… it’s more like I’m waiting for it to feel safe enough to stop. I do that with door locks too, and even old messages sometimes, which feels a little embarrassing to say.

Sometimes I count through the steps in my head, almost like if I get through them the right way then it’s okay. And if I try to stop before it feels complete, I get really anxious—panicky, honestly. There have been nights where I’ve stayed at the office for hours after everyone else left because I couldn’t make myself stop yet.

I know that probably sounds excessive. I’m just trying to answer honestly.
